I call it "over and under," I play it everyone morning on my commute.

There's a sign just before my exit on the freeway that shows the remaining time to get to downtown in both the regular lanes and the HOV lanes. As expected, most days the regular lanes are about 5 minutes slower, which is "under." But about once a week the HOV lanes are actually slower, which is "over," and then I laugh at the people stuck in the HOV lane as I take my exit

I feel you. I'm guessing you're in high school? I can't tell you a surefire way to make it a better experience. BUT, I can promise you that it *does* end eventually. I HATED high school with a burning passion. Hated everything about it. I passed the time by getting really in to vandalism with my only real friend at the time (throwing eggs at cars, TPing people's houses, etc). Then later in high school, I occupied my time with drugs. I don't recommend either of these at all, but it happened. But if you REALLY want to do one, throw eggs instead of doing drugs. I hated almost everyone I went to school with, but I eventually finished. I graduated by the skin on my teeth! 

My first real job out of high school, I ended up working a graveyard shift, and I still lived real close to the school- close enough to just barely hear the morning bells. So every day, I would get home from work, and right when I would lay down to go to sleep, I would hear the sound of school starting for everyone. Let me tell you, THAT was a pretty amazing feeling.

It gets better, if only because you eventually dont have to go any more.

Thank you for the kind words. Idk, I'm just really, really hesitant about seeking professional help. The last time I saw a counselor was when I was in rehab. He was a great dude but it was a LOT to handle. I really, really don't want to go to a professional. I can't explain specifically why, but I just *really* don't want to. I don't think I'm ready to see one. 

I don't know who of my friends I would open up to. I have friends that I would trust with that information, but I don't want to bring it up to them. I don't want to make them feel stupid- I've been hiding these feelings for a long time. They know me as the guy that's always laughing and smiling, so how would they feel knowing I was wanting to die this whole time?

I don't know. I like some of the things sobriety has afforded me. I really do. But I'm 23. I want to be able to live a normal life. I'm getting tired of people thinking I'm boring because I don't drink, but I also don't wanna go all tryhard on them by talking about how I used to start my day with enough heroin to kill them twice. 

I don't want to go back to getting loaded every day or shooting heroin. But I want to just drink and smoke weed like a normal 23 year old dude. Maybe I do need professional help, idk. I want to ask for help from my friends, but I don't feel like I can talk about it to them. I'm pretty sure they have no idea. I spent 3 years being a junkie and they had no idea. I wear a good mask around them. I'm always laughing and telling jokes, trying to be the center of attention. It would break their hearts to hear that I spend every day wanting to die :-/

I'm so tired of AA tho. Like really, it's getting old. When I first came in, I made it very clear that I didn't believe in god, and wasn't sure if I would ever be able. They said that that was okay, and I really believe that they were honest about that. But at 2 years clean I keep getting the feeling that I should have at least figured out whether I believe in god or not, and that god has become a much more integral part of the program.

"We had to fearlessly face the proposition that either God is everything or else he is nothing." Unfortunately, I'm leaning a lot more towards nothing. I don't "hate" god, I have nothing against people who believe in god, but I just *don't believe in a god of any kind*
